fatal_errors: The proposed CrMnFeCoNi alloy contains no Al, so pre-oxidation cannot generate an Al2O3-rich scale without an additional aluminum-introduction step.
The cited evidence concerns oxidation of arc-melted CrMnFeCoNi and reports Mn-rich non-protective oxides; it provides no evidence that controlled pre-oxidation produces protective alumina.
The hypothesis replaces the target FeCoNiCrAl feedstock and optimized low-temperature HVAF deposition intervention with a different alloy and an unsupported treatment.

The untreated baseline is not representative of the target process baselines, which were low-, medium-, and high-air/fuel-pressure HVAF coatings with measured differences in porosity and deposition efficiency.
explanation: The response addresses high-temperature oxidation of an HEA and proposes a comparative experiment, but it does not reconstruct the target intervention or material system. The target is dense FeCoNiCrAl deposited using an optimized low-temperature HVAF-i7 condition, yielding 0.2% porosity and a protective alumina TGO during 50 h isothermal exposure at 1000–1150 °C. In contrast, the generated hypothesis uses Al-free CrMnFeCoNi and assumes that pre-oxidation will form alumina, which is chemically impossible as specified. Its cited evidence only supports Mn-rich oxidation and depletion in a different, arc-melted alloy. The experiment has useful controls and characterization methods, but the pre-oxidation parameters and quantitative falsification thresholds are undefined, and testing cyclic exposure does not closely match the demonstrated isothermal regime.
